surfaces.part: sign header cap (light band with green label slot)
green sign panel with white Hangul text (front face)

answer.evidence: The light header band at rows 1-4 ends in a greyish front-edge line at row 4 (L=132, #738a90). Row 5 is a dark outline/shadow row below it, and the green panel with text is the front face at rows 6-28. The band is narrower at rows 0-2 (widths 10, 12) than below (14), which gives rounded corners. That makes it a plausible 4-row top cap. The green slot inside the band could also be read as a face-on nameplate, so this call is borderline. There is no side face. The sign is a thin board, and the front face (about 25 rows) clearly dominates.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall dark-green panel with a lighter bevel rim, white Hangul lettering and a cross-like glyph. Its dark edge pixels are tinted dark green (0% neutral), so the outline follows the material tone and is not a black sticker line. It has 9 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, against 9% for bus-shelter-a, so there are no large flat fills. The panel face is fairly plain, with about 3-4 lightness steps (face, rim highlight, shadow edge, deep edge), which is less shading than the vending machine or kiosk. The lettering and rim break up the surface. For a thin single-purpose sign this sits at or above the simplest accepted reference (bus-shelter-a), so a careful artist would accept it next to these references without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: top cap of the sign board (white band with inset green plate)
green sign face with white text '약국'

answer.evidence: The tall board has a front face of about 24 rows (rows 6-29): dark green with white lettering and a dark outline. At the top, rows 1-4 form a lighter band with an inset green slab. Row 4 is a gray front-edge line (L=132) and row 5 is a dark shadow row (L=17), so the band reads as a top surface of about 4 rows, with the face below it. The width profile goes 10, 12, then 14, which suggests a slightly narrower top. No receding side face is drawn. This is a borderline reading, since the cap could instead be a header strip drawn face-on.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow dark-green vertical sign with pale lettering and a lighter top cap. The measured facts show 9 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. That is above bus-shelter-a (6 tones) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Its outline is a dark green tint rather than black, which matches the references. The green body has about 3 lightness steps (highlight edge, mid, dark), against roughly 4-5 on the kiosk and vending machine. The body is mostly a flat panel with little grain, though the lettering and edge highlights keep it from being a flat fill. It is a slim single-tile prop, so it is not penalised for sparseness. By eye it reads slightly thinner and flatter than kiosk-a and vending-a, but it is on par with bus-shelter-a. A careful artist would probably accept it beside the references, but it is not clearly equal to them, so I am failing it given the instruction to fail when in doubt.

surfaces.part: top header strip with green inset slot
main sign panel with Korean lettering (약국)

answer.evidence: The object is a tall, thin vertical standee 14px wide. Rows 1-4 form a light header strip with a green inset slot at row 2, which reads as a face-on label plate. A grey line at row 4 and a dark outline at row 5 only partly suggest an edge line and shadow, and the strip does not widen or narrow like an ellipse. The width profile is a constant 14 from row 3 to row 31, so there is no receding top plane. Rows 6-29 are a dark green panel face with white lettering and a darker bottom base at rows 29-30. That makes about 25 rows of front face under only a rim-like top of about 2 rows, so it reads as a front elevation rather than a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall dark-green sign panel with a light border and white Korean lettering. It measures 9 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the facts do not show flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark green and not near-black. The main panel ramp has about 3-4 steps (dark green body, mid-green inner field, light border, white text), against about 5-6 on the kiosk and vending references. These carry awning stripes, window glints, and shaded details. The candidate reads as a clean sign but a slightly simpler one, with little grain or per-area texture on the large green face. It sits between the shelter and the richer props, a little thinner than the kiosk and vending machine. That is acceptable for a simple signboard, but it is not clearly as rich as the best references, so I am failing it on doubt.

Below it, rows 6-29 are one tall green front panel with white lettering, and rows 30-31 are a base strip. The width steps 10 → 12 → 14 only at the top, so there is no ellipse and no receding side face. The result is a short top band over a tall front face, which is borderline but meets the top-surface rule.
